# Run and compare

Run a model, compare scenarios and search for the best settings.

## naga examples

```text
usage: naga examples [-h] [--path]

List the models that ship in the package. A command that takes a model path
also takes one of these names: naga run single_server.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --path      print the folder they are in instead
```

## naga run

```text
usage: naga run [-h] [--version] [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--seed SEED]
                [--warmup WARMUP] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH] [--start ISO]
                [--until ISO] [--timezone IANA] [--workers WORKERS]
                [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--export FORMAT:PATH]
                [--player PATH] [--state FILE] [--no-logs]
                model

Run a Naga model headless.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.replications'
  --seed SEED
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        0 = run until the queue drains; default: the model's
                        own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --start ISO           real instant model time 0 stands for, e.g.
                        2026-01-05T06:00:00 ; overrides the model's own
                        'simulation.calendar.start'
  --until ISO           run until this real instant instead of a length; needs
                        a calendar start, from the model or from --start
  --timezone IANA       IANA timezone for --start/--until and for weekday
                        schedules (default: the model's own, else UTC)
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes, or 'auto'
                        (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the 10-sheet results workbook here
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --export FORMAT:PATH  write with a registered exporter, e.g. json:out.json;
                        repeatable. See nagasim.exporters.EXPORTER_REGISTRY
                        for the built-in formats (xlsx/csv/html/json/player)
                        plus any plugin ones
  --player PATH         write a shareable HTML player of the first replication
                        here: one self-contained file that replays the run in
                        a browser, with no server (the same as --export
                        player:PATH)
  --state FILE          start from this state document (`naga state take`):
                        the run's clock starts where the state was taken and
                        its statistics cover the run from there
  --no-logs             do not record the per-event entity/resource/store
                        logs: faster and much smaller on a long run, and every
                        summary statistic is unchanged -- only the three flat
                        log sheets come back empty
```

## naga scenarios

```text
usage: naga scenarios [-h] [--scenario SCENARIOS]
                      [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                      [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                      [--no-crn] [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--player PATH]
                      model

Run named scenarios headless and compare them.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIOS  scenario name to run (default: all); may repeat
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.replications'
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes, or 'auto'
                        (default: 1)
  --no-crn              disjoint seeds per scenario (Welch's interval) instead
                        of paired CRN
  --out OUT             write the comparison table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --player PATH         write a shareable HTML player here: the first
                        replication of every scenario, run again with its seed
                        and recorded, in one self-contained file with a
                        scenario switch
```

## naga invest

```text
usage: naga invest [-h] [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--seed SEED]
                   [--csv CSV]
                   model

Run every scenario and print payback, NPV and ROI against the baseline of the
model's investment section.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.replications'
  --seed SEED
  --csv CSV             write the table here as CSV
```

## naga fit

```text
usage: naga fit [-h] [--column COLUMN] [--top TOP] [--shift] [--json JSON]
                data

Fit candidate distributions to a data column.

positional arguments:
  data             CSV/TSV/TXT or XLSX file

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --column COLUMN  default: the first numeric column
  --top TOP        ranking rows to print
  --shift          fit a free location offset for positive-support families
  --json JSON      write the full ranking + best spec here
```

## naga doe

```text
usage: naga doe [-h] --factor FACTORS --response RESPONSE
                [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--design DESIGN] [--no-crn]
                [--surrogate {linear,quadratic,auto}] [--dataset DATASET]
                model

Run a design of experiments over model parameters.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --factor FACTORS      a factor, as 'path=kind:low:high[:step]' or
                        'path=cat:a|b|c'. kind is float/int/cat. Several
                        comma-separated paths before the '=' are driven with
                        the same value. May repeat. Example:
                        'resources.Agents.capacity=int:3:6'
  --response RESPONSE   the KPI key to analyse, e.g. 'system/Avg Throughput
                        Time'
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        replications per design point (default: 5)
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the result table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --design DESIGN       full[:levels] (default full:2), lhs:<n>, or oat
  --no-crn              give each design point its own seed block instead of
                        CRN
  --surrogate {linear,quadratic,auto}
                        fit a response surface over the design; included in
                        --report as its own section
  --dataset DATASET     write one row per (design point, replication) here, as
                        factors + responses + seed (.csv, or .parquet if
                        available)
```

## naga optimize

```text
usage: naga optimize [-h] --factor FACTORS --response RESPONSE
                     [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                     [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                     [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--goal {min,max}]
                     [--budget BUDGET] [--constraint CONSTRAINTS]
                     [--method {auto,pattern,optuna}]
                     [--indifference INDIFFERENCE]
                     [--min-improvement MIN_IMPROVEMENT]
                     model

Search model parameters for the best KPI within a replication budget.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --factor FACTORS      a factor, as 'path=kind:low:high[:step]' or
                        'path=cat:a|b|c'. kind is float/int/cat. Several
                        comma-separated paths before the '=' are driven with
                        the same value. May repeat. Example:
                        'resources.Agents.capacity=int:3:6'
  --response RESPONSE   the KPI key to analyse, e.g. 'system/Avg Throughput
                        Time'
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        replications per design point (default: 5)
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the result table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --goal {min,max}
  --budget BUDGET       total replications the search may spend (default: 300)
  --constraint CONSTRAINTS
                        a KPI constraint, as '<kpi key><=<value>' or '<kpi
                        key>>=<value>'. May repeat. Example:
                        'resource/Agents/Usage % (snapshot)<=85'
  --method {auto,pattern,optuna}
  --indifference INDIFFERENCE
                        the smallest difference worth detecting in the final
                        ranking-and-selection step (default: 5% of the best
                        mean)
  --min-improvement MIN_IMPROVEMENT
                        relative gain a move must reach before the search
                        widens that factor's step (default: 0.01 = 1% of the
                        objective). 0 widens on any significant gain
```

## naga policy-eval

```text
usage: naga policy-eval [-h] --policy POLICY --controller
                        {random,roundrobin,shortest}
                        [--reward {neg_wip,throughput,neg_time_in_system}]
                        [--episodes EPISODES] --horizon HORIZON [--seed SEED]
                        model

Evaluate a controller against a Policy-mode DECIDE.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --policy POLICY       decision-point name
  --controller {random,roundrobin,shortest}
                        built-in controller to evaluate
  --reward {neg_wip,throughput,neg_time_in_system}
  --episodes EPISODES
  --horizon HORIZON
  --seed SEED
```
